title: Cost-aware inference spike runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc defines an on-call runbook for detecting and investigating sudden inference cost spikes that impact customer billing or platform spend. Focus is on correlating billing signals (estimated token cost / minute) with runtime signals (batch size, KV cache heat, model fallbacks, queue length) and trace anchors that point to root cause (tenant, route, model variant, prompt shape).

Why separate cost-aware runbook?
- Traditional latency or error runbooks miss cost-only failures: e.g., a buggy reranking config that duplicates requests, a regression that increases average tokens per request, or a fallback storm to an expensive model.
- This runbook prioritizes quick cost containment while preserving signal needed for postmortem.

Key metric catalog (names used in dashboards/alerts):
- billing.estimated_token_cost_per_minute (USD/min) — upstream estimate derived from token counts and configured model pricing.
- inference.tokens_per_minute (tokens/min) — raw token emission across cluster.
- inference.requests_per_minute (rps) — request arrival rate.
- inference.avg_tokens_per_request — 1-min / 5-min rolling mean.
- inference.kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1) — fraction of requests served from warm KV cache prefix (tenant-scoped).
- inference.batch_size_p50/p95 — quantiles of batch sizes across serving queues.
- inference.model_variant_fallback_count — counts of fallback events to higher-cost variants or remote regions.
- inference.queue_depth_per_slot — pending queue length per serving slot/pool.
- tenant.cost_share_estimate — per-tenant rolling cost estimate (used for quick customer impact assessment).

Tracing anchors to collect in spans (span attributes to include in traces):
- trace.inference.request_id
- trace.inference.tenant_id
- trace.inference.route
- trace.inference.model_variant
- trace.inference.kv_cache_key_hash_prefix
- trace.inference.kv_cache_hit (true/false)
- trace.inference.batch_size
- trace.inference.latency_ms
- trace.inference.token_count
- trace.inference.fallback_reason (if fallback occurs)
Tip: ensure traces keep the first and last 3 token counts for large responses (sampling) so we can detect duplicated tail-looping.

Alert set (triage-first, cost-focused):
1) Cost spike soft (P2) — billing.estimated_token_cost_per_minute > baseline * 3 for 5m AND inference.avg_tokens_per_request increased by > 40% compared to baseline 1h.
2) Cost spike hard (P1) — billing.estimated_token_cost_per_minute > baseline * 6 for 3m OR tenant.cost_share_estimate for top-3 tenants shows >40% of cluster spend in 5m window.
3) Fallback storm (P1) — inference.model_variant_fallback_count > 50 in 10m AND fallback destination is a higher-cost model variant.
4) Duplicate-output loop (P1) — anomaly in trace token distribution: repeated identical prompt hashes and token counts across retries OR a sudden surge in request id replays (instrumentation flag: trace.inference.replay_detected=true).
5) KV-cold cascade (P2) — inference.kv_cache_hit_rate drops > 60% across pods and queue_depth_per_slot increases > 2x.

Alert routing and notification policy:
- P1 -> page the oncall (pagerduty) and post to #oncall-ops with the alert summary + top 5 tenants by tenant.cost_share_estimate.
- P2 -> notify #observability and create a FireTicket in JIRA with tags cost-spike and follow-up-required.

Immediate containment checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Step 0: Acknowledge alert and capture a screenshot of the billing panel and the last 30m of tokens_per_minute and avg_tokens_per_request.
- Step 1: Switch heavy throttles: flip the global soft-throttle flag for non-SLA customers (config path: config/ratelimits/global-soft-throttle). Reduce per-tenant burst window by 80% (safe default).
- Step 2: If fallback storm detected, toggle fallback-policy to prefer cheaper variant or disable cross-region fallback (config: routing/fallbacks/allow-elevated).
- Step 3: If duplication suspected, enable request de-dupe layer for the affected ingress path (feature flag: ingress-dedupe-enable). Add a short-lived 30s dedupe cache keyed on request fingerprint.
- Step 4: If KV-cold cascade: force an emergency cache-warm for top-5 tenants by generating synthetic prefix probes (scripts/warm-kv.sh) or route traffic to warm pools where caching is warm.
- Step 5: Communicate: post an initial notes message to #oncall-ops with indicators and containment steps taken. Tag product/responders for customer-impact assessment.

Investigation playbook (post-containment):
- Collect correlated windows: grab traces for the 15m prior to spike and 15m during spike. Query examples: 
  - trace query: service=runtime AND trace.inference.tenant_id IN (top-5) AND timestamp BETWEEN X and Y
  - metrics query: tokens_per_minute, avg_tokens_per_request, kv_cache_hit_rate grouped by tenant and route.
- Sift for behavioral signatures: 
  - rising avg_tokens_per_request with stable rps -> prompt length/regression.
  - rising rps with stable avg_tokens -> traffic engine or bot.
  - rising model_variant_fallback_count -> overload on preferred variant or misconfiguration in model weights.
  - repeat identical prompt hashes or identical trace signatures -> application-level loop.
- Examine deployment changes: look for recent rollouts (Console rollouts, PRs, commits) in last 24–72h that touched routing, reranker, or prompt templates. Linked PRs: check recent merges with tags routing/* or serving-runtime/* (use git log or GH PR search).
- Billing reconciliation: cross-check billing.estimated_token_cost_per_minute with actual queued billing export (billing-export job id). If mismatch > 10% investigate telemetry sampling logic.

Dashboard panel suggestions (compact set for rapid triage):
- Top row (quick triage): billing.estimated_token_cost_per_minute (1m, 5m windows), inference.tokens_per_minute, tenant.cost_share_estimate (top 10).
- Middle row (behavior breakdown): inference.requests_per_minute by route, inference.avg_tokens_per_request by route, inference.batch_size_p95.
- Bottom row (health signals): inference.kv_cache_hit_rate by pool, inference.model_variant_fallback_count by variant, inference.queue_depth_per_slot heatmap.
- Drill links: each panel should link to a trace query prefilled with time range and tenant IDs. Keep one-click link that opens the trace view with filter: trace.inference.fallback_reason IS NOT NULL.

Sampling and retention notes:
- Keep full traces for 48h for any request flagged with kv_cache_hit=false OR fallback_reason set (mark these for extended retention).
- Adaptive sampling: when cost-alerts trigger, temporarily raise sampling to 100% for the affected tenant(s) for 15–60 minutes to capture forensic data.

Post-incident items and metrics to watch after mitigation:
- Recompute baseline for billing.estimated_token_cost_per_minute and set a 2x and 4x anomaly threshold playbook based on week-over-week median absolute deviation (MAD).
- Create a gated rollout checklist for changes that can affect tokens_per_request (prompt/template changes, reranker rollout) requiring smoke tests with synthetic workloads and cost-estimates. Link: confluence:prompt-change-checklist.
- Add a dashboard widget that projects cost delta per change (estimate token delta * price) for PR descriptions.

Communications and customer follow-up:
- If tenant.cost_share_estimate shows a single customer >25% of spike: prepare an incident note for customer success with timeline, root cause, and cost remediation (crediting or waiver options).

Open questions and future work (notes to drive follow-ups):
- Can we instrument request fingerprinting earlier in the pipeline to detect duplication before it hits token accounting?
- Evaluate automated throttling policies per-tenant that are cost-aware (not just RPS-based) and can be enabled as a safety net.
- Explore a cold-cache pre-warming service for bursty tenants (predictive warmers).

Quick references and shortcuts:
- Slack: #oncall-ops, #observability
- Runbooks: confluence:observability-cost-playbook
- Scripts: infra/scripts/warm-kv.sh, infra/scripts/enable-soft-throttle.sh
- PagerDuty escalation: PD schedule: eng-oncall-primary
- Example JIRA template for follow-up: INF-XXXXX: cost spike postmortem (include impact, mitigation, root cause, action items).

Postmortem template (to paste into Jira):
- Summary: one-line description of the spike and impact.
- Timeline: minute-granular timeline of alert, containment, mitigation steps.
- Root cause: short description.
- Contributing factors: config changes, load patterns, sampling gaps.
- Detection: which alerts fired and why.
- Mitigation steps taken and why.
- Long-term fixes and owners (with deadlines).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working runbook; please validate the config keys and scripts referenced against infra repo and add missing run commands (Samir / Nora to confirm).

Last edited by: Maya Alvarez (eng-observability)
